# CIS AWS Database Services Benchmark — the OverWatch side of the map

**GENERATED by `scripts/cis_db_inventory.py`. Do not hand-edit.**

This is half of the mapping, and the half that needs no source document: what OverWatch
already asserts about the ten services the benchmark covers. **The other half is now
done** — see [`CIS_DATABASE_BENCHMARK.md`](CIS_DATABASE_BENCHMARK.md) for all 98
recommendations and the check that answers each, and `engine/aws_cis_db_map.py` for the
mapping as data. This file remains the per-check view: the benchmark document is organised
by recommendation, and this one by what OverWatch ships.

The "Proven" column comes from `docs/CHECK_FIRING.md`: `yes` means the suite drives the
check to a real FAIL. A check that runs but has never failed is not evidence of coverage,
which is the distinction that whole document exists to keep.

> **On the source document.** CIS Benchmarks may not be redistributed and the PDF is not
> in this repository. What is cited here is a section number and a recommendation COUNT,
> both references; every description is generated from this product's own catalogue.


## 2 — Aurora

*11 recommendations in the benchmark. OverWatch ships 8 check(s) against this service.*

| Check | Severity | Proven to FAIL | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUR-01` | HIGH | yes | Full disclosure of the entire cluster's data if any storage artifact is exposed, and a data-at-rest compliance failure spanning the whole cluster. |
| `AUR-02` | MEDIUM | yes | Irreversible loss of the entire cluster and its data from one API call -- a catastrophic availability and data-loss event. |
| `AUR-03` | HIGH | yes | Exploitation of known, unpatched engine vulnerabilities across the cluster leading to data compromise or takeover, plus forced extended-support costs. |
| `AUR-04` | CRITICAL | yes | The entire cluster database contents disclosed to any AWS customer worldwide -- an immediate, authentication-free data breach. |
| `AUR-05` | HIGH | yes | Plaintext cluster data exposed on share, copy, or leak -- a data breach and an encryption-at-rest compliance failure. |
| `AUR-06` | HIGH | yes | Any client configured without TLS connects to the cluster in cleartext, exposing credentials and query results to anything on the network path. |
| `AUR-07` | MEDIUM | yes | Anything discovered later than the retention window cannot be restored, and for a cluster left at the default that window is one day. |
| `AUR-08` | MEDIUM | yes | Access depends on long-lived static passwords that are copied into application configuration, rarely rotated, and revocable only by rotating them everywhere. |

## 6 — MemoryDB

*7 recommendations in the benchmark. OverWatch ships 6 check(s) against this service.*

| Check | Severity | Proven to FAIL | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MDB-01` | HIGH | yes | Credentials and authoritative data cross the network in cleartext, readable with ordinary packet capture by anything with a network position. |

| `MDB-03` | MEDIUM | yes | There is no recovery from an accidental flush, a bad write or a destructive action -- and no way to rebuild the cluster with different settings. |
| `MDB-04` | LOW | yes | No key policy to audit, no attributable key-usage trail, and no way to revoke access to the data by disabling the key. |
| `MDB-05` | MEDIUM | yes | Published engine vulnerabilities remain unpatched indefinitely, because nothing prompts anybody to apply them. |
| `MDB-06` | MEDIUM | yes | An availability-zone failure removes the whole datastore, and without cross-AZ replicas that is potential data loss rather than downtime. |

| `DOCDB-06` | HIGH | yes | Client connections carry credentials and document contents in cleartext across the VPC, readable by anything with a position on the network. |

- **51** OverWatch checks speak to those services today.
- The two numbers are NOT comparable: one check can answer several recommendations, and several recommendations are not decidable at all. Producing the actual per-recommendation mapping is the point of the mapping pass; this file is its left-hand column.

## Declined, with reasons

Recorded as data in `engine/aws_cis_db.py` so this file and the coverage test read the same list.

- **`keyspaces-needs-a-data-read-grant`** — Amazon Keyspaces authorises its control-plane reads -- ListKeyspaces, ListTables and GetTable -- under cassandra:Select, and that is the SAME action that authorises reading table rows. AWS offers no metadata-only read action for the service, so covering it would mean adding an action to the scanning role that permits reading customer data. That crosses the read-only-of-CONFIG line this product's role is built on, and which tests/test_perm_ledger.py::test_the_additive_policy_contains_only_read_actions already enforces by excluding s3:GetObject and logs:StartQuery for exactly the same reason. The checks themselves would be straightforward -- pointInTimeRecovery.status and encryptionSpecification.type are both plain enums -- so this is a decision about the GRANT, not about feasibility. If it is ever wanted, it belongs in an opt-in permission block alongside the other data-plane reads rather than in the default policy

- **`qldb-everything`** — Amazon QLDB has NO service model in the pinned botocore at all -- boto3 cannot construct a client for it, so none of section 11 is buildable regardless of whether it would be worth building. AWS removed the service from the SDK. tests/test_cis_db_keyspaces_timestream.py asserts this rather than asserting the judgement, so if AWS ever restores the model the decision gets re-made instead of silently standing

- **`timestream-database-key-ownership`** — whether a Timestream database uses a customer-managed key or the AWS-managed one cannot be told from the API. Every database returns a KmsKeyId, and for the AWS-managed key that is still an ARN in the customer's own account with the same shape as a CMK -- there is no field distinguishing them and no alias in the response to match on. Guessing from the key id would be wrong in both directions

- **`elasticache-cluster-mode`** *(readable, judged not a finding)* — whether Redis cluster mode (sharding) is enabled is an architecture choice, not a posture setting -- a single-shard replication group is a legitimate and very common design, so reporting it would flag correct systems. The availability properties the recommendation is reaching for are covered by ELC-04 (automatic failover) and ELC-08 (Multi-AZ), which are settings rather than architecture
